this isn't a real perf test, just a nontrivial amount of assembler generated. This also may not reflect our build, I'm not sure what the default template params for std::shared_ptrs locking policy are in arm-gcc
What's the next step here? Testing?
top on alon8 shows that with 50 some sensors, we're still using 1% of the CPU. Its not breaking the bank.

?  "lock" is not a multiprocess lock.  It is a conversion from weak_ptr to shared ptr.  It is not blocking, and poorly named.

I'm not sure what we're looking at in godbolt, but this should be fine.  It's a pattern used all over in dbus-sensors.
Ack.
Do we really need weak pointer here? Can shared pointer be used here instead, since this function is not recursive unlike `GpuDevice::read`? Same for all other Sensor classes.

If we use shared_ptr, then the NvidiaGpuTempSensor will now own itself, and it will effect shutdown negatively, because NvidiaGpuTempSensor can't be destroyed until the callback comes back, which might never happen if the io is shut down.
